task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 11, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update about Threadgate Stores' change to paid opening work and the separate review of earlier time records.

facts.text: Threadgate Stores announced Tuesday, Aug. 11, 2026, that employees assigned to opening preparation will begin paid shifts 15 minutes before doors open.
The change begins Sept. 7 at the chain's 18 clothing stores.
Opening preparation includes unlocking stock cages, checking tills and taking delivery racks onto the sales floor.
The old scheduling system commonly placed the paid start time at the public opening time, according to the company's internal review.
The company estimates that correcting earlier time entries could result in $84,000 of additional pay, but individual calculations are unfinished.
The review covers opening shifts from January 2024 through June 2026 and approximately 260 current and former workers.
Threadgate said former employees will be contacted at their last recorded address and may submit updated contact details through its payroll office.
The company has not announced a date for completing every payment calculation.
The new schedule does not change base hourly wage rates or the public opening hours of stores.
Payroll director Oren Tal said managers will receive additional labor-budget hours rather than being told to cut later shifts to cover the change.
Employees began raising the scheduling issue after a new till system recorded the time of the first morning check.
The till timestamps show when checks occurred, not every task performed before opening.
Employee representative Anya Bell said workers want access to the records used in their individual calculations.
Threadgate says employees will receive an itemized calculation and can request a payroll review if they disagree.
Bell said, "Starting the clock earlier fixes tomorrow. People still need to see what happened to yesterday."
Tal said, "Opening the shop is work, even when there are no customers in it yet."
The company has not published a store-by-store breakdown of the estimated additional pay.
The reporting record contains no court judgment or regulator finding about the old scheduling system.
Threadgate began as a single workwear shop in 1996 and now sells school uniforms as well as adult clothing.
The review concerns opening preparation; it does not purport to settle every possible time-record issue across the chain.

forbidden_additions: A final $84,000 payout already distributed or a completed payment timetable
A court ruling, regulatory finding or settlement of all payroll disputes
